The first public release of Aero: a local LLM bootstrapper for Windows, Linux and macOS. It scans your PC, picks a model that fits, installs the right llama.cpp build for your GPU, tunes it, and gives you a local agent that can use your files, shell, screen, apps and browser.

## Install

| System | File | Then |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Windows** 10 / 11 (64-bit) | `Aero-windows.zip` | Extract it, double-click `Update-Aero.bat`, accept the admin prompt. Installs into `C:\Aero`, with Start menu and desktop shortcuts and an entry under Settings → Apps → Installed apps. |
| **macOS** (Apple Silicon or Intel) | `Aero-macos.zip` | Unzip it, right-click `Install-Aero.command` → Open. Adds `~/Applications/Aero.app`. |
| **Linux**, any distro | `install.sh` | `curl -fsSL https://github.com/NermalYT/Aero/releases/latest/download/install.sh \| sh` |
| Debian, Ubuntu, Mint, Pop!_OS | `aero_1.0.0_all.deb` | `sudo apt install ./aero_1.0.0_all.deb`, then run `aero` or use the app menu. |
| Fedora, RHEL, Rocky, Alma, openSUSE | `aero-1.0.0-1.noarch.rpm` | `sudo dnf install ./aero-1.0.0-1.noarch.rpm` (openSUSE: `sudo zypper install ./aero-1.0.0-1.noarch.rpm`) |
| Arch, Manjaro, EndeavourOS | `PKGBUILD` | `makepkg -si` in a folder holding the `PKGBUILD` |
| Any Linux, by hand | `Aero-linux.tar.gz` | Extract it and run `sh Aero/install.sh` |

`SHA256SUMS.txt` lists the checksum of every file. The Linux installer finds your package manager (apt, dnf, zypper, pacman, apk, xbps, eopkg, emerge, swupd or Homebrew), shows the command before installing anything missing, and never needs to run as root.

## What's in it

- **A regular Windows app.** Aero is listed under **Settings → Apps → Installed apps** with its icon, version and size, and **Uninstall** there removes it completely: the app, its Python environment, llama.cpp, models and chats (two boxes let you keep models or chats), the shortcuts, temporary files and the entry itself.
- **Updates from GitHub.** Aero checks for a newer release once when it starts, never in the background. **Update now** downloads it, verifies the checksum and installs it. Models, chats, memory, settings, mods and tunings are kept.
- **Mod Aero.** Describe a change to Aero in plain words and your local model makes it in a copy of Aero's code. Aero compiles it, runs its tests and starts a test copy before you can apply it, shows the diff, and can turn it off or undo it. A mod that breaks startup is undone automatically, and mods carry over to new versions.
- **Forever-loop journal.** After every round of the ∞ Loop the model writes down what worked, what didn't and what to do next, and the next round starts from that.
- **Models learn from each other.** Aero records which tools worked or failed on each task and which model ran them. When something fails or you give feedback, the model writes short notes. Any model you load later gets the notes from similar tasks, and every model knows your stated preferences. You can see and delete all of it under Settings → Memory.
- **Agents and subagents**, with a dashboard listing models, agents and subagents.
- **"*Model* is controlling *app*"** header and banner, each with a Stop button, whenever a model clicks, types or opens apps.
- **Fits any PC**: NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Apple Silicon or CPU only, with VRAM-aware tuning and a CPU router model.
- **Local Only: On / Off**, next to the ChatGPT, Claude and Loop buttons. On, the model answers by itself with no web search, browser, MCP servers or cloud reviews. Off, it searches and reads the web when a task needs it.
- **Optional ChatGPT and Claude review passes** that teach your local model, and **strict offline** mode that blocks every non-local request.

Full list: [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/NermalYT/Aero/blob/main/source/CHANGELOG.md).

## Tested so far

- 118 automated tests pass on Linux and on Windows 11.
- On Windows 11: the Installed apps entry and the uninstaller, end to end (listed by Windows and winget; uninstalled with the exact command Settings runs; keeping or deleting models and chats; stopping a running copy; removing shortcuts and the entry; refusing folders that aren't Aero).
- Installs from these release files passed on Ubuntu 24.04 and 22.04, Fedora 42 and Arch Linux, plus AlmaLinux 9 and Alpine with the llama.cpp step skipped (containers, no GPU).
- A real self-update from this release to a newer one kept a user's mod.

**Not tested yet:** a full Windows install with a GPU, macOS installs, GPU speeds, and real ChatGPT and Claude calls. Details are in the [validation report](https://github.com/NermalYT/Aero/blob/main/source/docs/VALIDATION_REPORT.md). Please open an issue if something goes wrong.
